lessons.title: Lent and Easter
lessons.idea: Lent is a time to pray and share. Easter is a time of joy because Jesus rose.
lessons.question: How can we share with others?
lessons.activity: Make a Lenten bank for the poor. Decorate an Easter egg with a cross.
teach: Lent: forty days of prayer, sharing and small sacrifices (CCC 1438). Easter: Jesus is alive! (CCC 540, 1169).
Alleluia returns at Easter.
Small promises that match a child’s age.
talk: What can you share this Lent?
Why do we celebrate at Easter?
How can you help someone in need?
quiz: Easter is when…|The Church began|Jesus was born|Jesus rose from the dead|The apostles were chosen|2|Luke 24.
In Lent we pray, fast and…|Buy toys|Sleep|Complain|Give to the poor|3|Matthew 6:1-18.
lessons.life: Put coins in a Lenten box for the poor each week.
lessons.saint: Mary Magdalene: the first person to see Jesus alive on Easter morning.
lessons.mem: Alleluia! Jesus is risen!
lessons.hook: Show a bare branch and a flower. “Lent is quiet. Easter is joyful.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What do we do in Lent? What do we say at Easter?”

script.open: Start by hiding a toy under a cloth. “I have something to show you, but first we have to wait.” After a minute, lift the cloth. “Waiting makes it even better. The Church does that with Lent and Easter.”
teach: Say: “Lent is the time before Easter. It is forty days. We pray more, we give to those who need help, and we try to say no to things that are not good for us. It is a time to get ready to celebrate that Jesus rose from the dead.”
Tell: “On the first Easter morning, some women went to Jesus’ tomb. The stone was rolled away. The tomb was empty! An angel said, ‘He is not here. He has risen!’ (Luke 24) Jesus was alive!”
Say: “That is why Easter is the happiest day in the whole year. We say ‘Alleluia!’ again, the church is full of flowers, and we celebrate. Lent is a quiet time. Easter is a joyful time.”
ask: What do we do during Lent? (Pray, share, say no to things.)
What happened on Easter morning? (Jesus rose from the dead.)
What is a word we say at Easter? (Alleluia!)
practice: Give each child a small cup or a paper bank. Say: “This is our Lenten bank. When we do something kind or give up a treat, we put in a coin to help the poor.”
Decorate a paper egg with a cross and bright colors.
Hold the eggs up and shout, “Alleluia! Jesus is risen!” Cheer.
Put the eggs on the wall as a bright display.
script.close: Sign of the Cross. Say: “Jesus, thank you for rising for us.” Send home: “Start saving coins for the poor.”

tryit: Put a coin in the Lenten bank each time you share.
Decorate an egg with a cross.
Say: “Alleluia! Jesus is risen!”
lessons.saintStory:
Mary of Magdala was one of the women who followed Jesus and helped to take care of him and his friends. Jesus had set her free from great trouble, and she loved him very much.
She stayed near the cross when most of the friends of Jesus ran away. On the morning of the third day she went to the tomb very early, while it was still dark. The stone had been rolled away, and the tomb was empty. She stood weeping, and then a man spoke her name, “Mary.” She turned and saw it was Jesus! She ran to tell the disciples, “I have seen the Lord!” That is why she is sometimes called the “apostle to the apostles.”
Mary Magdalene shows us what Easter joy is like. The sad time of Lent turned into the greatest news ever told: Jesus is alive.

lessons.title: Ordinary Time and Thank You
lessons.idea: Ordinary Time is the time of green, when we grow like plants in God’s love.
lessons.question: What helps a plant grow?
lessons.activity: Plant seeds in cups and watch them grow. Pray, “Help me grow, Lord.”
teach: Ordinary Time is green, the time of growing in God’s love (CCC 1163, 1168). Seeds and plants fit the parables.
Plant seeds and watch them grow.
Say thank you for the little things.
talk: What helps a plant grow?
What helps us grow in love?
What are you thankful for?
quiz: Green is the color of…|Easter|Ordinary Time|Lent|Advent|1|Liturgical colors.
We grow in love by…|Prayer and kindness|Fighting|Hiding|Winning|0|Colossians 3.
lessons.life: Water a plant with your family and thank God for the gift of life.
lessons.saint: Thérèse of Lisieux: she called herself a “little flower” and taught the little way of love.
lessons.mem: Thank you, God, for helping me grow.
lessons.hook: Show a green plant. “Green means growing.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What color is Ordinary Time? Why?”

script.open: Bring a small plant in a pot and a seed packet. Ask the children, “How does a seed grow?” Take answers (water, sun, soil, time).
teach: Say: “After Christmas and Easter, the Church has a long season called Ordinary Time. The color is green, like grass and leaves. Green is the color of growing. In Ordinary Time we grow, like plants, a little at a time, in God’s love.”
Read Psalm 1:3: “Like a tree planted by streams of water.” Say: “A tree grows tall when it has good water. We grow when we pray, go to Mass, are kind and listen to Jesus.”
Say: “Growing takes time. It does not happen in one day. Every day we can do small things: say a prayer, help someone, say thank you. And God helps us grow, as a gardener cares for the garden.”
ask: What color is Ordinary Time? (Green.)
What does a plant need to grow? (Water, sun, soil.)
What do we need to grow close to God? (Prayer, Mass, kindness.)
practice: Give each child a clear cup, a spoonful of soil and a bean or other seed.
Help children plant their seeds and water them gently.
Write their names on the cups.
Put the cups in a sunny spot and check them each week.
script.close: Say: “Help me grow, Lord.” Say the grace after meals: “We give thee thanks, almighty God.” Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Look at your seed and say thank you each day.”

tryit: Plant a seed in a cup.
Water it a little.
Say: “Help me grow, Lord.”
lessons.saintStory:
Thérèse of Lisieux was a young French girl who became a Carmelite nun when she was fifteen. She was not famous or powerful. She felt small, like a little flower in God’s garden.
She wrote that she could not do great things, but she could do small things with great love: smile at a grumpy sister, say thank you, or do a chore quietly. She called this her “little way.” She was very sick for a long time, but kept trusting God. She died when she was twenty-four.
Thérèse is a saint, and a Doctor of the Church. She shows us that in Ordinary Time, when nothing special happens, we can grow in love like a little plant.
